# Film-mode integration seams — behaviour notes for runtime code (2026-10-13)

Written by the hooks lane after implementing SPEC §4 items 1–8 in the existing scene3d files
(`git diff HEAD -- scene3d/index.js scene3d/cells.js scene3d/entities.js scene3d/statics.js
scene3d/particles scene3d/animated_scenery.js scene3d/atmosphere_pipeline.js`; suite `tests/film_hooks.test.mjs`).
Runtime modules under `scene3d/film/runtime/` must code against exactly these names and behaviours.

## Exported seams

- scene3d/index.js: reads `liveScene3d.film = {preFrame(tsMs, dt), postRender(), holdLoop}` (installed by film code); `window.__renderOnce(tsMs?)` → true; only with `?filmMode=on`: `Promise.all([import("./film/index.js"), import("./particles/particle_manager.js")])` → `installFilmMode({liveScene3d, THREE, sessionHandle, wasmExports, particleCull: {setParticleCullConfig, allParticleManagers}})` (particle_manager.js is the same module instance entities.js / statics.js load)
- scene3d/cells.js: honours `scene3d.filmViewer = {cell}` OR `window.liveScene3d.filmViewer = {cell}` (cell 0 or absent = off)
- scene3d/entities.js: `EntityManager.prototype.setFilmHidden(guid, on) → boolean`; `EntityManager.prototype.clearAllFilmHidden() → number`; instance term `inst._filmHidden`; remembered set `em._filmHiddenGuids`
- scene3d/statics.js: marker `staticsGroup child .userData.__filmHidden = true` (Mesh/InstancedMesh/LOD)
- scene3d/particles/particle_manager.js: `export function allParticleManagers() → ParticleManager[]`; `export function setParticleCullConfig({maxDistance, recheckInterval}) → {maxDistance, recheckInterval}` (previous values); render-only `emitter.filmHidden = true`. Consumers (through `particleCull`): take_player cullBegin/cullEnd set `recheckInterval: 1` for every rendered take and restore only the interval; scout stills do the same; particles_query enumerates with `managers: allParticleManagers`
- scene3d/particles/particle_fx.js: `export function setFxTimeSource(fn|null)`; `export function setFxNearFadeMin(m) → previous`; `FX_UNIFORMS.uFxNearFadeMin` (default 0)
- scene3d/animated_scenery.js: `export function setSceneryTimeSource(fn|null)`
- scene3d/atmosphere_pipeline.js (only with `?filmDof=on`): `window.__dof = {get/set enabled, get/set target (THREE.Vector3 by reference | [x,y,z] | {x,y,z} copied | null), get/set focusDistance (finite ≥ 0, metres, Euclidean distance from the camera), get/set focusRange (finite > 0), get/set bokehScale (finite ≥ 0), get effect}`; `pipeline.filmDof` (the effect); `createAtmospherePipeline(..., {filmDof: boolean})` test override

## How to use them (timing, restore, pitfalls)

- camera_owner / film_clock: install `liveScene3d.film = {preFrame(tsMs, dt), postRender(), holdLoop}`. preFrame runs inside tick() after `liveScene3d.frameTime` is stamped and before tickPerFrame, with the tick's own ts and dt. postRender runs synchronously after the final draw on EVERY render exit, including the portal-space, nullRender and direct paths; that is where the VideoFrame must be created. Both are try/catch'd (one `[film]` warn).
- film_clock stepping: set holdLoop = true, then call `__renderOnce(base + k*1000/fps)` with strictly increasing timestamps. Take `base` from `liveScene3d.frameTime.tsMs`, not the wall clock: a gap over 0.5 s from the last frame freezes dt to 0 for 11 frames unless renderOnDemand is on. fps < 10 clamps dt to 0.1. A timestamp below the last one gives a negative dt (not clamped). The first explicit-ts call under holdLoop cancels any pending rAF or pacer re-arm. tick is async under syncPhysicsTick, so `__renderOnce` returns before the frame finishes: await your postRender promise. film_clock's step() publishes the frame time, then yields one animation frame (rAF; 50 ms setTimeout fallback; one MessageChannel task on a hidden page or with no rAF) BEFORE `__renderOnce(ts)`. The first step's yield lets the pre-hold re-arm run; it parks on holdLoop and the clock re-bases past it. end() waits past lastTs (and, under `?particleClock=sim`, past the film particle time), clears holdLoop, and calls bare `__renderOnce()` only when the realtime chain is dead (a step issued an explicit-ts render, or `frameTime.tsMs` changed since begin). Otherwise the still-pending pre-hold re-arm resumes the loop; a second re-arm would run two rAF chains.
- Time sources: `setFxTimeSource(() => filmMs)` sets uFxTime = (ms/1000) % 1024; repeated identical stamps are no-ops. `setSceneryTimeSource(() => filmMs)` re-bases on every swap; the scenery driver is still paced by its own rAF and clamps dt to 0.1 s. For stepped takes that clamp loses nothing: the clock yields one rAF per film frame, so the scenery driver advances exactly 1/fps per film frame, except on the 50 ms fallback path, where it catches up on the next callback. Restore both with null.
- Viewer cell: publish `scene3d.filmViewer = {cell}` or `window.liveScene3d.filmViewer = {cell}` (both work). A non-zero cell roots the wasm walks via setViewerCell and is published to viewer_cell.js. Delete it, or set cell 0, on release; the player-head walk then resumes on the next frame. `camera_owner.parkCell()`, called by world.teleport (only when no take, prepare, shoot, rehearse or scout runs), deletes `filmViewer` while the camera stays owned, so the next site loads with the player-head walk's viewer state; the next camera write re-seeds the cell (the plan cell after `setCutCell`, else the player-head walk).
- Hides. Entities: `entityManager.setFilmHidden(guid, true)` hides the rig and its wielded children, and it casts no shadow. Its held SetLights and its particles (which live in entitiesGroup) still render: use `emitter.filmHidden` for those. The guid is remembered, so call `clearAllFilmHidden()` at the end of a take. Statics: set `userData.__filmHidden = true` on top-level staticsGroup children (Mesh, InstancedMesh, LOD), and also `visible = false` to cover `?frustumCull=off`; restore both. BatchedMesh nodes need `setVisibleAt`. Particles: `emitter.filmHidden = true` is render-only and the simulation continues. `setParticleCullConfig` returns the previous values: restore them after the take.
  How take_player's pilot fades use the statics seam for PLACED tree / prop occluders (LandBlockInfo statics; fade keys from world_query `describeHit`, resolved by `staticFadeTargets`). v1 never fades procedural scenery: a scenery collider hit carries no fade key (the wasm CollisionHit names no placement, and geometry alone keyed the wrong one on real data — a false clear view through a boulder), the sensors drop any id on a scenery hit, and `staticFadeTargets` resolves a scenery key to nothing, so the take hides nothing and takes the reroute bias (SPEC §3.1; v2 needs a placement index on CollisionHit from the wasm scenery sweep). For a placed occluder: a per-placement node (Mesh / LOD / animated anchor, or an InstancedMesh holding only that placement) gets `userData.__filmHidden = true` + `visible = false`; one instance of a shared InstancedMesh gets a zero 3×3 at its own origin + `needsUpdate`, restored only if still unchanged. A BatchedMesh instance gets `setVisibleAt(id, false)`, and the take re-shows it only if three things hold: no other owner called `setVisibleAt` on it during the take (while it holds a hide, the take shadows that mesh's `setVisibleAt` with a pass-through watcher, removed after the last release); the instance is still hidden; its geometry id and matrix are unchanged. Residual: writes that bypass `setVisibleAt`, or a frozen mesh, fall back to the state checks only. animated_scenery's instanced anchors honour `anchor.visible = false` (`_anchorVisible` collapses their slots). `safety.release()` runs BEFORE take_player restores its fades (reverse order of application), and `fade()` never adopts an emitter that is already `filmHidden`.
- Static catalogs (read-only): film/index.js builds world_query's `catalogs` with `createStaticCatalogs`. It READS scene3d/vfx_catalog.js `vfxDescriptorFor(did)` (dynamic import of the same module instance the client's own VFX paths fill: the statics bake and the entity spawns — tipFlex, weaponFx, gemSparkle; never `ensureVfxCatalog`, never writes or loads the catalog) for each placement's archetype (tree vs rock: a label for scenery, the fade rule's kind for placed statics) and DAT-bounds size, and calls wasm `fetchSetupSelectionSphere(setupId)` once per uncatalogued Setup DID (prefetched per landblock, boxes freed; each prefetch waits at most 3 s, and a DID still unsettled when a wait times out is remembered as stalled and never waited for again). A `staticsNear` query loads its landblocks concurrently, so it waits about one 3 s bound in total, not one per landblock. An optional collider source (`createStaticCatalogs({colliderOf})` → `staticColliderOf(did)`) feeds the scenery hit LABEL rule (never a fade), but none is wired: the VFX descriptors carry no collider data. Flag off: neither happens; vfx_catalog.js is not modified. Only the client's own VFX paths load the catalog: the statics bake for the GPU tree sway (default on; off with `?treeWindGpu=off`, `?treeWind=on`, `?windGeo=on` or `?visual=off`) and for the `?windGeo=on` wind peel, which has NO `?visual` gate (statics.js calls `ensureVfxCatalog()` under `windGeoEnabled()` alone); entity spawns for `?tipFlex`, `?weaponFx` and `?gemSparkle` (each default on under `?visualAll`, all off under `?visual=off`). So the catalog stays empty exactly when `?windGeo=on` is absent and either `?visual=off` is set or every other path is off (GPU tree sway off and `?tipFlex`, `?weaponFx`, `?gemSparkle` all off, e.g. `?treeWindGpu=off&visualAll=off`). Then scenery reads as rock (a label; it never fades in v1 either way) and a placed tree reads as a prop sized by its selection sphere, if any, so it fades only when that known size passes the small-prop rule; otherwise the pilot reroutes.
- Sun: film/index.js reads `liveScene3d.skyLightingController._lastState` (fallback: one `sessionHandle.getSkyState()`, copied, then freed) and imports scene3d/night_ramp.js `nightFactorFromAuthoredPitch` (night ≥ 0.5 → no sun). SkyState `dirHeading` / `dirPitch` are DEGREES, the heading clockwise from +Y north toward the sun (the pkg d.ts "radians" comments are wrong; every consumer reads degrees). `worldQuery.subject().velocity` (the per-guid position history) feeds the live subject's reference track.
- AdminEnvirons (read-only; no environ_override.js / loop.js change): (1) `window.__environOverrideState()` (loop.js:1375) returns `environOverride.stats()`: `{active, option, name, transition, fogT, lightT, sets, fogTicks, lightTicks, nextFogTick, fogTickSec, …}`. (2) loop.js adopts a NEW `__environFogOverride` object identity only on its next frame (the sync sets transition to 0), so look.js keeps the object when the fog is unchanged. (3) The fog tick runs every 0.8 s and the light tick every 15 s, both on `performance.now()` wall time, each stepping the transition by +0.04: the roll-in takes about 18–21 s. (4) With the 'Disable distance fog' option on, only the light tick syncs and steps. (5) `__setTerrainLightScale(__terrainLightState().scale)` invalidates the light tick, so the next frame re-lights. (6) `?environRetail=off` snaps the fog on (film never sets it). take_player polls (1) before every rendered take, forcing (5) once the fog has settled, for at most 30 s (report `environ`).
- DoF: `window.__dof` exists only with `?filmDof=on` AND when the composer pipeline was built, so typeof-guard it. Drive `focusDistance` every frame from the Pose `focus` channel (metres, Euclidean distance from the camera). Alternatively set `target` (a THREE-world Vector3, kept by reference; AC→three is [x, z, -y]); while enabled it overrides focusDistance each frame. focusRange must be > 0, bokehScale ≥ 0; invalid values throw RangeError or TypeError. Set `enabled` in look/prepare before recording, never per frame (each flip recompiles). For the best defocus, boot with `clouds=on` (split chain); the default legacy single pass defocuses the pre-aerial scene.

## Deviations from the SPEC text (binding: the code is the contract)

- DoF idle state: the effect uses BlendFunction.DST while `__dof.enabled` is false, and its update() is skipped. The spec allowed opacity 0 or bokehScale 0; the WIP used opacity 0. pmndrs EffectPass leaves a DST effect out of the compound shader entirely, so `?filmDof=on` with DoF idle produces the same GLSL, samplers and pass list as the flag off (asserted in H8c). With opacity 0 the 4 samplers and texture fetches would sit in the shader for every film frame. Cost: flipping `enabled` recompiles the owning EffectPass once each way, so toggle it between shots, never per frame; a write that does not change the value is ignored. pmndrs never removes stale defines and uniforms, so after enable→disable the DoF's renamed keys stay unused in the material: the GLSL is identical and costs one extra compile.
- DoF placement follows the spec (legacy fxPass list after horizonDissolve; split-chain postEffects ahead of fxGlow/bloom). CAVEAT for the legacy single pass: pmndrs effects' update() reads the pass input, so defocused pixels show the scene from before this pass's aerial perspective and horizon dissolve; a fully defocused far background loses its haze. The SSAO composite also lands after the DoF there. The split chain (`?clouds=on`, cloudsMainPass on by default) defocuses the finished atmosphere and late particles correctly. Documented in the code comment.
- Removed the WIP's production test seam `_sceneryNowMsForTest()` from animated_scenery.js. The test uses harness/lib/import_edited.mjs to append a probe export (`_nowMs` / `_rafLastMs`) to the shipped module instead.
- Additions beyond the spec text: (1) `__renderOnce(tsMs)` cancels a re-arm still pending from before the hold (`_cancelSchedule()`), but only when holdLoop is set and the timestamp is explicit, so no wall-clock tick lands between film steps. (2) `setSceneryTimeSource` re-bases `_rafLastMs` on every swap, avoiding a clamped 0.1 s jump or a frozen frame when the time base changes. (3) preFrame and postRender calls are wrapped in try/catch with a single `[film]` console.warn, so a throwing hook never kills the loop or skips scheduleNext. (4) `setFilmHidden` remembers guids, so a respawned or rebuilt rig comes back hidden; `clearAllFilmHidden` forgets them. (5) `opts.filmDof` boolean override on createAtmospherePipeline, matching the existing `opts.*` test overrides.
